query: If the most common operational burdens described in the text were eliminated, how much would resolution duration drop?

per_column.name: operational_burden
per_column.rationale: Categorizes each ticket by the type of operational burden from short_description, giving a genuine grouping axis directly relevant to identifying the 'most common' burdens the query asks about. Row samples (WiFi, VPN, Database, printing->Other) are sound readings of the source text.

per_column.name: burden_reduction_percent
per_column.rationale: Values are perfectly correlated one-to-one with operational_burden category (each category maps to a single fixed percent), making it largely a redundant restatement of the category. Moreover the specific percentages (32, 30, 28...) are not derivable from any information present in the table; they appear to be invented assumptions with no textual support.

per_column.name: estimated_duration_reduction_minutes
per_column.rationale: This is the quantity the query ultimately calls for, so it is on-axis. However it is derived by multiplying an ungrounded fabricated percentage by a duration, and the table samples do not even expose closed_at/resolution duration in evidence, so the specific minute values assert a confident precision the source does not support.

judge.rationale: operational_burden is a strong, well-grounded categorization that directly serves the query's need to identify common burdens. The two quantitative columns, however, rest on fabricated per-category reduction percentages with no basis in the table's content; burden_reduction_percent is also essentially a deterministic restatement of the category. As a set, the useful analytical axis is present but the numeric magnitudes central to answering 'how much would duration drop' are ungrounded inventions.
